name: September 11 attacks
kicker: 2001 al-Qaeda attacks on the U.S. · Deadliest terrorist attack in history
briefing: On the morning of September 11, 2001, 19 al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four airliners. Two struck the Twin Towers of New York City’s World Trade Center, which both collapsed; one hit the Pentagon, near Washington, D.C.; and the fourth crashed in a Pennsylvania field after its passengers fought back. The attacks killed 2,977 people, making them the deadliest terrorist attack in history. Two memorial pools, opened in 2011, mark where the towers stood.
answerHtml: September 11 attacks (or 9/11; prompt on descriptions like an attack on the World Trade Center or the Twin Towers; do not accept “1993 World Trade Center bombing”)
prompt: attack on the world trade center
attacks on the world trade center

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: The New York Philharmonic asked composer John Adams to write _On the Transmigration of Souls_ in memory of the people killed in this event. That piece premiered about a year after this event and won the 2003 Pulitzer Prize for Music.
tossups.r: In this event, hijacked planes destroyed the Twin Towers in New York City. For 10 points, name these 2001 terrorist attacks.

tossups.p: The musical _Come From Away_ tells how the small town of Gander, Newfoundland, welcomed thousands of stranded airline passengers whose flights were diverted to Canada during this event. That day, every civilian plane flying over the United States was ordered to land at the nearest airport.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these attacks in which al-Qaeda hijackers crashed planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: A 2004 report on this event blamed a “failure of imagination” and recommended creating a Director of National Intelligence to oversee the nation’s intelligence agencies. Former New Jersey governor Thomas Kean chaired the commission that wrote that report, and Lee Hamilton was its vice chair.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 terrorist attacks that destroyed the Twin Towers in New York City.

tossups.p: An official report called Khalid Sheikh Mohammed the “principal architect” of this event; he was captured in Pakistan in 2003 and later held at the U.S. prison at Guantánamo [“gwahn-TAH-nuh-moh”] Bay, Cuba. His nephew, Ramzi Yousef, had planned a 1993 truck bombing of one of this event’s targets.
tossups.r: Mohamed Atta led the 19 hijackers in this event. For 10 points, name these al-Qaeda attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: During this event, President George W. Bush was listening to a class of second-graders read a story called “The Pet Goat” at Emma E. Booker Elementary School in Sarasota, Florida. His chief of staff, Andrew Card, leaned over and whispered that “America is under attack.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks in which hijackers flew planes into the World Trade Center.

tossups.p: Three days after this event, President George W. Bush climbed onto a pile of rubble and answered rescue workers through a bullhorn: “I can hear you!” That year, _Time_ named New York mayor Rudy Giuliani its Person of the Year for leading the city’s response.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 terrorist attacks in which hijacked airliners struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: The Tower of Voices, a memorial near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, holds 40 wind chimes, one for each passenger and crew member killed when their plane crashed in a nearby field during this event. Those passengers had learned through phone calls about the other attacks and decided to fight back against the hijackers.
tossups.r: That plane was United Flight 93. For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks that also struck the Pentagon.

tossups.p: A Callery pear tree nicknamed the “Survivor Tree” was pulled from the wreckage after this event, nursed back to health, and replanted at a memorial designed by Michael Arad. That memorial, called _Reflecting Absence_, has two square pools that sit in the footprints of two destroyed skyscrapers.
tossups.r: Hijacked planes had struck those towers. For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: Bronze panels around a memorial’s pools list 2,983 names, including six people killed in a 1993 bombing at the same site. That memorial was dedicated on the tenth anniversary of this event, in 2011, and a museum beneath it opened three years later.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks, which killed 2,977 people in New York, Virginia, and Pennsylvania.

tossups.p: A memorial in Arlington, Virginia, opened in 2008 with 184 benches, one for each person killed at a nearby military headquarters during this event. Most of those victims worked inside that building, and the rest were aboard American Airlines Flight 77.
tossups.r: That building was the Pentagon. For 10 points, name these 2001 terrorist attacks, which also destroyed the World Trade Center.

tossups.p: Once nicknamed the “Freedom Tower,” a skyscraper built after this event rises exactly 1,776 feet to honor the year the Declaration of Independence was signed. When it opened in 2014, it was the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.
tossups.r: It stands at the rebuilt World Trade Center. For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks that destroyed the original Twin Towers.

tossups.p: For the first time in its history, NATO invoked Article 5, which says that an attack on one member is an attack on all, the day after this event. Less than a month later, the United States and its allies began a war to drive the Taliban from power in Afghanistan.
tossups.r: Osama bin Laden, the al-Qaeda leader behind this event, was killed in Pakistan in 2011. For 10 points, name these al-Qaeda attacks on the United States.

tossups.p: About six weeks after this event, President George W. Bush signed the USA PATRIOT Act, which expanded the government’s power to watch and investigate suspected terrorists. In 2002, Congress combined 22 agencies into a new Department of Homeland Security, first led by Tom Ridge.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: In Jonathan Safran Foer’s novel _Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close_, nine-year-old Oskar Schell searches New York City for the lock that fits a key left by his father, who died in this event. Paul Greengrass directed _United 93_, a 2006 film about one of the planes in this event.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks in which hijacked airliners hit the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

tossups.p: The New York City Fire Department lost 343 of its members in this event, including its chaplain, Father Mychal Judge, who was officially listed as the event’s first recorded victim. For months afterward, workers searched and cleared the site, which became known as Ground Zero.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name these 2001 attacks in which two hijacked planes destroyed the Twin Towers.

trap.title: 1993 or 2001?
trap.body: The World Trade Center was attacked twice. On February 26, 1993, a truck bomb exploded in a parking garage beneath the North Tower, killing six people; that bombing is a different answer line, even though its victims’ names are also on the memorial. Many questions also mention Osama bin Laden or al-Qaeda early, and a player who blurts out the man or the group instead of the event loses the tossup.
trap.fix: Hijacked airliners, the Pentagon, Flight 93, Shanksville, and 2,977 victims mean 2001; a truck bomb, an underground garage, and Ramzi Yousef mean 1993. Listen for the noun: “this event” or “these attacks” wants the attacks, “this man” wants Osama bin Laden, and “this group” wants al-Qaeda.
trap.line: Real answer line: September 11 attacks (or 9/11; do not accept “1993 World Trade Center bombing”)
